question: How long does a typical data engineering project take, and how many people work on it?

ranking.text:
## Data Engineering
We build cloud data pipelines, warehouses and lakehouses. Typical work includes migrating legacy reporting databases to a modern cloud warehouse, building automated ingestion, and setting up data quality checks. Delivery is usually done by a small squad of two engineers and one lead over eight to twelve weeks.

## Results after six months
Reporting time fell from four days to under one hour. Report disputes dropped by roughly 70 percent. The project ran as a fixed-scope engagement of ten weeks, followed by a monthly managed service.

## The challenge
Clinic managers built weekly reports by hand from five separate systems. Reports arrived four days late and the numbers rarely matched.

## Best-fit customers
Mid-market and enterprise companies in healthcare, financial services and retail, with 500 to 5,000 employees. They already collect data but report from scattered spreadsheets and ageing databases. The buyer is usually a Chief Data Officer, VP of Analytics or Head of Operations, with a named budget for data modernisation.

## Buying signals
Recent cloud migration announcements, new data leadership hires, regulatory reporting pressure, and public job postings for data engineers.

## Applied AI and Machine Learning
We design forecasting, classification and recommendation models, and retrieval-augmented assistants that answer questions from a client's own documents with citations. Every model ships with monitoring and a handover guide so the client team can run it.

## Lessons
Agreeing KPI definitions in week one avoided most late rework. The client's own analysts were trained to maintain the pipelines.

## Poor-fit customers
Very small companies with no data team, and organisations that only want staff augmentation with no outcome ownership.

## What Kai's Company did
We delivered a cloud data warehouse with automated nightly ingestion, defined twelve shared KPIs, and launched an executive dashboard. A pilot assistant let managers ask questions about the reporting policy handbook and receive answers with page citations.

## Analytics and Dashboards
We create executive dashboards, KPI frameworks and self-service reporting. We define each metric once so that every team sees the same numbers.

## Delivery modalities
Engagements run as a fixed-scope project, a monthly managed service, or a time-and-materials team extension.

## Competitive positioning
Large consultancies offer breadth but are slower and costlier. Offshore body shops are cheap but rarely own outcomes. Kai's Company competes on small senior squads, fixed-scope pricing and a clear handover. We do not claim to match the scale of the largest firms.
